The standalone term heading is absorbed into the tracking-plan-item terminology and its retained definition; no separate decision is lost.
The term heading is absorbed into the concrete-item definition retained by S010 and S011.
The term heading survives as the logical_artifact field and the explicit logical-artifact definition.

activation.note: The resolved configurable root, every JSON item regardless of change status, and the root-or-acceptance adoption gate match the source. Task terms are contextual cues rather than exceptions to the explicitly stated all-item scope. The adoption finding is explicitly labeled as needing a new observer; file and path facts are directly observable.

audit.summary: All source knowledge survives across the claimed destinations, including schema constraints, cross-artifact checks and the adoption exception. The then clause has one identity-mirroring obligation; the other constraints remain explicit in guidance and evidence, and the shared strict-disposition node is genuinely generic. Application-specific names occur only in the preserved reference example, not as activation conditions or coder requirements.

segmentChecks.note: The bundled requirement is distributed without loss: resolved-root JSON scope, path grammar, schema validation, path-derived identities and cross-file id uniqueness all remain explicit.
The term heading has no independent obligation; its meaning survives in the retained tracking-plan-item definition.
The heading is absorbed into the explicit concrete-item URN definition and measure rules.
The heading survives through the logical_artifact field, formula and explicit definition.
The term heading is absorbed into the telemetry_root configuration and resolved-root guidance.
Strict disposition remains in audit, and the genuinely generic shared node preserves fail-on-every-finding behavior with no advisory mode or ratchet baseline.
All required and optional item fields survive in prefer[1] and verifier_detail[4], including forbidden_properties and metric-only dimensions.
The mandatory metric measure and prohibition for event, trace and log items are stated in coder guidance, evidence and verifier detail.
The default telemetry/ root, topology.telemetry_root override and versioned-source-of-truth role are retained; configured-root replacement is also explicit.

URN grammar, SemVer core version, and property classification/cardinality survive in verifier_detail[2]. However, prefer[1] says only 'SemVer version', creating a coder-facing ambiguity rather than a destination loss.
Both required-names subset properties and global concrete-id uniqueness remain explicit in coder guidance, evidence and verifier detail.
The no-root/no-acceptance-declaration gate, no-findings behavior and protection of non-adopting repositories during upgrade are retained.

risks: prefer[1] says 'SemVer version' rather than the canonical 'SemVer core version'; a weak coder could accept prerelease or build metadata instead of requiring the core X.Y.Z form unless they consult the schema or verifier detail.

The unless clause equates adoption with 'making the first acceptance decision' but does not tell a weak agent how to recognize or locate an acceptance telemetry declaration, so applicability can be misjudged.

unobservable: finding=telemetry_adopted is explicitly needs_new_observer; a Datalog engine currently has no fact from which to derive root existence or an acceptance telemetry declaration.

review.summary: I agree with the auditor's PASS: the compressed headings, shared strict policy and sampled normative knowledge are preserved at their destinations. The rewrite is largely actionable, but its coder-facing SemVer wording is weaker than the canonical core-version requirement, and deterministic activation awaits an adoption observer.
